name: Bicervical Bicornuate Uterus and Blind Hemivagina
aliases: Obstructed Hemivagina and Ipsilateral Renal Anomaly (OHVIRA) Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for OHVIRA Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of bicornuate uterus with two distinct cervical canals (bicervical uterus)
Blind hemivagina causing unilateral vaginal obstruction
Ipsilateral renal agenesis or dysplasia associated with uterine and vaginal anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of bicervical bicornuate uterus with blind hemivagina on imaging or surgery
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Renal anomalies support diagnosis but are not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral hematocolpos due to obstructed hemivagina
pathognomonic.notes: Accumulation of menstrual blood in obstructed hemivagina
searchTerms: blocked vaginal hemivagina causing blood collection
one-sided vaginal blockage with menstrual blood buildup

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bicervical uterus detected on imaging or surgery
searchTerms: two cervices seen on imaging or surgery
painful menstruation starting after first period
pain in lower belly or pelvis
missing or malformed kidney on same side

common.symptomName: Pelvic mass palpable on physical examination

occasional.symptomName: Urinary tract infections related to renal anomalies

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific laboratory markers
imaging: Ultrasound showing bicornuate uterus and hematocolpos
MRI pelvis confirming bicervical bicornuate uterus and blind hemivagina
Renal ultrasound or CT showing ipsilateral renal agenesis or dysplasia
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; considered a congenital Mullerian duct anomaly
other: Surgical findings confirming uterine and vaginal anatomy

distinguishingFeatures: Single cervix instead of bicervical uterus
Rudimentary horn may or may not communicate with main uterine cavity
Normal uterine anatomy with vaginal septum causing obstruction

redFlags: Severe unilateral pelvic pain with hematocolpos
Recurrent urinary tract infections with renal anomalies
references: Rock JA, Zacur HA. Mullerian Anomalies and Their Management. Obstet Gynecol Clin North Am. 2017;44(3):495-507.
